item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:964 initially calls runFix(l,null,"tests"); :619 defaults target to "code"; :624 chooses test vs component source from that target. item.observed: Business logic and calculations: if a test patch times out or cannot match, Try again sends the same test issues against the main component implementation, presents a main-code diff, and Accept changes the component, not the test. The automatic recovery route can alter valid production code and never repairs the test. Developers can cancel/reopen the original test Fix as a workaround, but the erroneous accepted output can materially change the system.
reproduction_steps: Open Tests with a reported missing include.
Press Fix and encounter a timeout or patch_failed response.
Press Try again.
Inspect the second request/review: its .cpp is now the component implementation.
Accept: main C++ changes while the test file is unchanged.
item.surface: Tests > Fix these > error > Try again
item.title: Retrying a failed test fix can patch the component instead — Retry drops the tests target

item.evidence: fixLog.js:35 defines at(i) using h.added.every(...); for a deletion h.added is [], so this is always true. :36-37 accepts the original h.start unconditionally for empty added, then :43 inserts h.removed there. No surrounding context is stored in hunk(:13) or verified.
item.expected: R-333/request: undo "just that fix", "even if the code above has shifted"; "If the lines changed since ... nothing changes". For a deletion, identify the original gap from anchored context or refuse ambiguity, never insert at an unrelated stale line.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: undoing a fix that only deleted lines after another change inserts lines above that gap restores the removed code at the old numeric position, potentially inside another function/declaration. Repeated Undo also inserts the deleted block repeatedly because the empty added sequence always matches. This produces materially incorrect C++ while reporting success; only manual review or a whole-version restore recovers it.
reproduction_steps: Accept/save a fix deleting a block of code at line 20.
Apply another fix inserting five lines above line 20, leaving the deletion's neighborhood otherwise untouched.
In History choose the deletion fix > Undo this fix.
The removed block is inserted at line 20 rather than the shifted location at line 25; invoking Undo again inserts it again.
item.surface: History > past deletion fix > Undo this fix
item.title: Undoing a deletion can insert code into the wrong function or duplicate it — empty added hunks match any old line number

item.evidence: fixLog.js:4-13 combines all changes in a file into one span and independently slices removed and added to MAX=400; makeFixEntry :22 stores these truncated spans, FixDetailModal.jsx:93-95 displays them, and undoFixEntry :43 replaces only the truncated added span with truncated removed.
item.expected: request/R-331/R-333: "Show every accepted fix ... before/after again" and "undo just that fix". Retain the complete changed content or reject a history entry too large to undo safely; do not silently truncate an operation.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: for supported imported/long code with two changes more than 400 lines apart, history omits the second change. If the first change adds a line, Undo replaces 400 added lines with 400 removed lines whose endpoints differ, drops an unchanged boundary line, and leaves the later change applied. It reports success despite corrupting source and not undoing that fix. The 40k/60k API code bounds permit this workload.
reproduction_steps: Import a system whose .cpp exceeds 450 short lines.
Accept one fix adding an include near the top and changing another line beyond line 450.
Save and View the fix: the latter edit is missing.
Undo this fix: only the truncated prefix span is replaced, not the whole accepted operation.
item.surface: Fix History for long C++ files
item.title: Long fixes cannot be accurately viewed or undone and can damage code — history silently truncates each file's change span to 400 lines

item.evidence: emailer.py:116 calls _assert_safe_email outside the try at :118. :72-74 raises ValueError on any listed substring, including 'cvv'. teams.py:131 commits the invite before :132 send_invite; team names flow into subject/body at :83-87. projects.py:417-419 similarly commits then sends.

The owner gets an error rather than the invite result/fallback guidance; retry updates its role without sending because the member already exists. item.evidence: teams.py:125 reads members then :131 unconditionally $pushes a new member when absent; :139 role changes use positional members.$ (first match). projects.py:414-418 and :427 have the same read-check-push/first-update pattern. The owner is unable to revoke edit authority with the role control despite a successful downgrade response. Removing the member entirely can recover safely but is not the requested Viewer access.

Have that email's password account accept the link from the second stored invitation.
Change the member to Viewer.
That account's next save still derives Editor from its unchanged user_id-bound entry.
item.surface: Team/project Invite and role downgrade endpoints
item.title: A downgraded teammate can retain Editor access — concurrent invites create duplicate memberships and role changes update only the first

item.evidence: emailer.app_url(:95) derives the trusted email link host directly from x-forwarded-host or host, with no configured-origin comparison. auth.py:279 embeds that URL plus the reset token in the actual email sent at :280. _assert_safe_email(:79-83) permits any ordinary HTTPS hostname. server.py:740-751 installs no host-validation middleware.
item.expected: R-284/request: reset link "opens the app's reset page directly"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: server-derived authority stays authoritative; checklist, Third-party integrations: requests must "leak nothing." Use a trusted configured app origin or an explicitly trusted/validated proxy host for sensitive links.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: if the ingress preserves a caller-supplied forwarded-host header (or permits arbitrary Host), an unauthenticated forgot-password caller can make the real reset email direct the recipient's single-use token to a different HTTPS site. A recipient following that authentic-looking email exposes the token there, allowing account takeover and access to their projects. The source lacks host enforcement; whether the deployed proxy overwrites those headers is not available, so reach is conditional on that stated ingress behavior, not runtime-tested.
reproduction_steps: On a deployment that forwards caller-supplied forwarded-host values, request a password reset for an existing account while supplying a different HTTPS hostname via that header.
Inspect the app_url/template path: the emailed reset link uses that hostname, not the app origin.
If the recipient follows it, the token is delivered to the other site's reset URL.
item.surface: POST /api/auth/forgot-password; invite email URL construction
item.title: Reset recipients can be sent to a foreign site with their token — email URLs trust an unvalidated request host

item.evidence: BundleModal.acceptBatchFix(:97-107) awaits the save without setting pending/consumed state; FixReviewModal:76 leaves Accept enabled. Each handler then calls advance(:115); :79 calls requestFix for the next project, which records usage/server.py:564 and sends a provider request/:566.

Optimistic versioning prevents the second write (409), but both handlers then start the next project's paid fix request, consuming two requests for one review. One competing result can replace the other, and the user sees a spurious save-conflict error. Main data is not double-saved, but quotas and review order are impaired.
reproduction_steps: Start Fix all projects for at least two projects with issues.
In the first project's review, double-click Accept and save new version before the save completes.
Both handlers proceed to the next project and each sends a fix request; one earlier save gets a 409.
item.surface: Bundle > Fix all projects > Accept and save new version
item.title: Double-clicking batch Accept spends two requests on the next project — acceptance stays enabled during save and advances twice

item.surface: Workspace Tests/Team navigation and center editor at 375px
item.title: Phone users cannot reach the Tests workflow — fixed 660px sidebars consume a 375px viewport with overflow hidden

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:774 only pre-fills saveNote when it is currently blank; cancel at :1154 only closes the modal. Toast Undo(:679-681) removes fixNotes/fixLog but not saveNote. openProject(:378-382) likewise clears fixNotes/fixLog but leaves saveNote unchanged.
item.expected: R-313: "undoing the fix removes its note from the next save's pre-fill"; R-314 stores the user's final note for the correct version; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: context restoration must retain the correct object. Reset/recompute automatic prefill on undo and project change while preserving edits only for the same draft.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: after opening then canceling Save, an auto-filled fix note is frozen in saveNote. Undoing the fix or opening another project does not clear it, so the next Save shows and can persist a claim about a fix no longer present or performed on another project. Users can manually edit the short note, making this inexpensive but misleading history friction.
reproduction_steps: Accept a fix, press Save to see its pre-filled note, then Cancel.
Undo fix from the toast and press Save again: the old Fixed note remains.
Alternatively open another project before pressing Save: the previous project's note is still there.
item.surface: Save note dialog after Cancel + Undo or project switch
item.title: Undoing a fix can leave its old save note attached to another version — pre-filled saveNote is not cleared with fix state

item.evidence: restoreVersion(:460-463) replaces project/system via openSystem but never clears fixLog/fixNotes. openSystem(:354-372) does not clear them either. saveProject(:330) submits fixLog for the next snapshot, and exportZip(:437) reports it as fixes since last save.
item.expected: R-331/R-332: each version lists fixes "accepted before that save" for its actual code; request: restoring a version replaces unsaved fixes. checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: state changes propagate consistently to histories and reports.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: restoring an older version after an unsaved accepted patch discards its code but leaves the patch in Not saved yet and auto-fill notes. The next save associates the discarded fix with the restored code, and exports report a fix no longer applied. The restored code itself is correct, but history/audit and selective undo are misleading.
reproduction_steps: Accept an unsaved fix on a saved project.
Restore an earlier version using Compare.
Open History: the discarded fix is still under Not saved yet.
Save or export: its fix entry/note/report accompanies code that no longer contains it.
item.surface: Compare > Restore version > History/Save/export
item.title: Restoring old code keeps discarded fixes in pending History and reports — restore never clears fixLog or fixNotes

item.evidence: saveProject(:333-337) guards setProject by savingFor, but :339-342 unconditionally closes the current save dialog and clears saveNote/fixNotes/fixLog even after a project switch. openProject(:380-381) starts the next project's independent fix queues; its new entries can then be cleared by this earlier response.
item.expected: request (inherited fix): "Save ... results can no longer land on a project you switched to"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; R-313/R-331 require accepted fixes/notes to remain until their own save.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: while A's slow save is pending, the user can open B and accept a fix. A's completion clears B's unsaved fix history/automatic note despite correctly leaving B's project metadata alone. The B code remains patched, but its accepted-change record is irrecoverably missing from the next version unless the user reconstructs it. Saving remains disabled during A's request, but Fix controls are not.
reproduction_steps: Save project A while its network response is delayed.
Open B and accept a fix before A's save returns.
When A's save succeeds, B's fixLog and fixNotes are emptied.
Save B: its patch has no corresponding history entry or automatic note.
item.surface: Cross-project async Save completion and Fix History
item.title: A late save erases the next project's unsaved fix history — completion guards metadata but clears global fix state unconditionally

item.evidence: FixReviewModal.jsx:71-72 displays both data.cpp_header and data.cpp_source for test fixes. Workspace.jsx:1175 supplies the current header for that review, but :646 Accept only copies data.cpp_source into tests.code and silently ignores data.cpp_header. The normal code branch :657 copies both.
item.expected: R-294/request: tests "can be fixed the same way" through the before/after review; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: material actions must apply exactly the reviewed approved changes. Enforce header read-only at the endpoint/review boundary, or apply a supported header edit explicitly and track it.
item.observed: AI and model features: if the model proposes a header-only repair or a paired header/test change, the user sees and accepts both diffs, yet the header remains unchanged. For instance a proposed visibility correction allowing a test to call a component method is never applied, so that test still cannot compile despite the accepted review. This is conditional on the model response and was not executed.
reproduction_steps: Request a Tests fix whose provider response changes the header as well as the tests (the endpoint accepts either file).
Review the displayed header/source changes and press Accept fix.
Only the tests source is installed; the approved header edit is discarded with no error.
item.surface: Tests > Fix > before/after review > Accept fix
item.title: Test-fix review can promise header repairs that Accept silently drops — test acceptance applies only the returned .cpp

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:570 exportIssues comprises main activeIssues plus AI review only. :426-427 gates warnings on it and :440 passes it to badge calculation; :438 separately reports testIssues, proving known test errors exist. BundleModal.jsx:15-18 checks only checkSystem; :117 computes shared=bundleIssues(plan), but :124-125 sends only checks to report/buildBundleZip. zipExport.js:205/:326 grants a badge if those incomplete lists lack errors.
item.expected: request: badge when "No errors, warnings allowed"; R-307: "every current issue (errors and warnings)"; R-340 bundles export tests too. No-errors/report calculations must include all known errors in shipped files and bundle compatibility.
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: a project with clean main C++ but a missing AutomationTest.h test error exports without warning and gets a no-errors badge; bundles also omit those errors from reports. Additionally two individually clean systems with duplicate reflected class names show an explicit bundle conflict, yet the README can say no errors and COMPILE_REPORT omits it because shared conflicts never enter checks. Developers receive misleading compile status for a zip the app already knows has errors. No Unreal build was executed.
reproduction_steps: Export a system with clean main C++ and Tests reporting a missing AutomationTest.h error: no export warning appears and README says no errors.
Bundle it with another project: the test error is absent from the bundle report.

Alternatively bundle two individually clean systems declaring the same class: UI shows a duplicate-class error, but README's aggregate badge and COMPILE_REPORT still use only the clean per-project lists.
item.surface: UE5 .zip export warning/README badge; bundle compatibility/report
item.title: Exports claim no errors despite known test or bundle errors — warning, report and badge inputs omit whole issue sets

item.evidence: teams.py:156 rejects an already-used invite only when user_id differs, and :160 leaves invite_token intact. projects.py:448-451 uses the same different-user-only condition. AuthPages.jsx:105-108/:81-84 treats any 200 as a fresh join success.
item.expected: R-267 and R-076 explicitly require refusal on a second use and single-use invitation links. Consume the token, returning an already-used refusal for replay while preserving the existing membership.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: the same signed-in invitee can replay the link indefinitely and receive You joined success every time. This does not create duplicate memberships or grant a different account access; the demonstrated consequence is inaccurate invitation lifecycle/status, rather than an established security compromise.
reproduction_steps: Accept a team or project invitation as its addressed account.
Open that same invite URL again.
The endpoint returns success and the page announces another join instead of the requested used-link refusal.
item.surface: /team-invite/:token; /invite/:token
item.title: Used invitations keep announcing a fresh join — accept handlers retain tokens and permit same-account replay

item.evidence: teams.my_teams(:35) sorts oldest first and to_list(100), then project_roles_via_team(:41) authorizes projects using only that truncated set. projects.py:187 caps team project rows at 1000 and :295/:306 cap preset lists at 200. No continuation cursor/count is returned and ProjectsPanel.jsx:28-29 builds the switcher only from the returned teams.
item.expected: R-263: GET teams returns "exactly the teams the caller belongs to"; R-337: users may belong to several teams; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation." Authorization must not use a truncated listing as the complete membership set.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a user belonging to 101 teams loses the newest team from the switcher and loses project access through it because authorization reuses only the oldest 100 memberships. Similarly older presets and excess team projects silently disappear without paging. This is a growth-boundary prediction, not measured workload behavior; the demonstrated main harm is inaccessible listed work/membership, recoverable through reducing collections or direct-sharing projects but not through a next-page control.
reproduction_steps: Create or join more than 100 teams; create a project in the newest team.
Reload Projects > Team: that team is omitted from the oldest-first result.
A non-owner whose only access is that team gets Project not found on the project's GET because the role map excludes it.
For presets/team projects, exceed their result caps: no next page or truncation notice is available.
item.surface: Team switcher, team project authorization/listing and Bundle presets list
item.title: Growing team collections silently hide work and can revoke valid access — capped membership lists are reused for authorization

item.evidence: sideBySideDiff(:49) allocates (n+1) Uint16Arrays of (m+1) entries and :50-53 fills every cell. FixReviewModal:10 computes the whole diff before limiting display context at :11-18. server.py:512-513 allows up to 40k/60k characters, and projects.py:108 accepts imported system dictionaries without line bounds.
item.expected: checklist, Performance and resource leaks: bound transformations and tie work growth to supported payloads; request: before/after review must remain usable for accepted source. Compute bounded hunks or otherwise avoid quadratic full-file allocation for a small patch.
item.observed: Performance and resource leaks: importing a valid long .cpp with 20,000 short lines (within 60k chars) then reviewing a tiny fix builds about 400 million two-byte cells (~800 MB, plus row objects) and performs 400 million iterations synchronously on the UI thread. Filtering to nearby changed lines happens afterward and saves no work. This predicts serious browser unresponsiveness/memory pressure exactly when users must approve/discard, not an observed latency measurement.
reproduction_steps: Import a C++ system with a source containing roughly 20,000 short lines within the supported 60k-character fix bound.
Request and receive a small patch.
Open its review: FileDiff computes the entire 20,000 by 20,000 LCS matrix before rendering a few changed lines.
item.surface: Before/after fix review and Compare diff for long imported C++
item.title: Small fixes to long files can stall the review window — full-file quadratic diff runs before context filtering

item.evidence: FixReviewModal.jsx:44 supplies onDiscard as Modal.onClose; Modal.jsx:6/:11/:15 calls onClose on Escape/backdrop/X. Workspace.jsx:1177 invokes exportZip(thenExport,true) whenever that handler runs for a non-running auto-fix review/error.
item.expected: R-317: "no zip downloads before one of [Accept fix and export or Discard and export] is pressed"; request: auto-fix must "Show the before/after review first"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: cancel/close must respect the user's interruption instead of completing an unrelated action.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: closing an auto-fix review or error with X, Escape or the backdrop downloads the unpatched zip immediately, even though the user did not choose either export action or Export without fixing. They can delete the unwanted download and restart, but cancellation does not work as the dialog affordance promises.
reproduction_steps: Enable Auto-fix before export and choose a plugin export with issues.
Wait for the fix review or error.
Press X/Escape instead of an export button.
The close handler forces export of the unpatched system.
item.surface: Auto-fix-before-export review/error > X, Escape or backdrop
item.title: Closing auto-fix review downloads a zip instead of canceling — modal Close is wired to Discard and export

item.evidence: zipExport.js:176-177 writes the original header/source (only retargeting API on header); :178-183 separately adds tuning helper files and CSV. unrealExtras.js:127 defines ApplyTuningRow but :165-167 instructs users to manually add a BeginPlay call. No table property or read is injected into the component. Workspace.jsx:981 renders only result.setup_guide, not tuning.setup.
item.expected: request: "The generated code reads its defaults from that table when one is assigned" and "The Setup guide gains steps for importing the table and assigning it"; R-304/R-305 require matching parameter names and actual component initialization with built-in fallback and Why notes.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: for an ordinary system with tunables and no existing DataTable initialization, the exported component never reads the CSV/table. Designers must author extra Blueprint wiring instead of assigning a table, and the in-app Setup Guide omits this workaround. Numeric keys normalized by pascal (e.g. regen_rate -> RegenRate at :96) also only apply if a component property happens to have that exact name. Essential generation/export remains available, but the promised no-code tuning integration is missing.
reproduction_steps: Generate/open a component with numeric tunables but no DataTable property or initialization call.
Open Setup Guide: there are no added DataTable steps.
Export the plugin and inspect the original component and added TuningLibrary: only the library contains the table-reading logic.
Import the CSV in Unreal; assigning/creating a table alone cannot change this component's defaults without manually adding the helper call.
item.surface: Plugin export Data Table and Setup Guide
item.title: Assigning a tuning table does not initialize the generated component — export adds an uncalled helper instead of table-backed defaults

item.evidence: planBundle(zipExport.js:271-273) resolves module collisions by suffixing the second module; writeModule(:184) calls blueprintClipboard(system) without that resolved module. unrealExtras.js:48 always builds classPath using moduleName(system), which returns the unsuffixed name.
item.expected: R-293/R-341 and request: "Pasted nodes reference the generated C++ classes, so they work after the plugin is built." The class reference must name the module actually written to Source and declared in the bundle .uplugin.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: two otherwise distinct supported projects such as HealthComponent and HealthSystem both normalize to HealthKit; the bundle correctly names the second runtime module HealthKit2, but its Blueprint paste text references its class under HealthKit. That class is in a different script package, so the second system's generated calls/variables cannot resolve as promised. The C++ modules themselves are still exported; this is a bounded Blueprint artifact failure, predicted from source without Unreal execution.
reproduction_steps: Bundle distinct projects whose header bases are HealthComponent and HealthSystem and whose graphs call their generated methods.
Inspect module planning: Source/HealthKit and Source/HealthKit2 are emitted.
Inspect HealthKit2's Blueprint file: generated class references still use /Script/HealthKit rather than HealthKit2.
item.surface: Bundle plugin > second module's Blueprints/*_EventGraph.txt
item.title: Blueprint calls in renamed bundle modules point to the wrong class package — clipboard export ignores the resolved unique module name

item.evidence: toggleAutoFix(:609) sends each PATCH independently and :610 applies every response to current project without pending disable/sequence/project check. Checkbox :762 remains enabled while requests run. Backend/projects.py:280 writes each boolean with no version or operation ordering.
item.expected: R-315/R-316: per-project state shared with teammates; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "repeated toggles preserve the chosen state" and stale responses must respect later decisions. Retain the user's latest selection and bind responses to the intended project.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: rapidly turning auto-fix on then off can leave it on if the first request is delivered/processed last. A late response after opening another project also sets that new project's local auto-fix display to the old project's value, though its backend setting was not changed. Users can recover by reloading and re-toggling, but may launch an unwanted paid fix based on misleading state.
reproduction_steps: Toggle Auto-fix before export on and then off while the first request is delayed; allow the on request to finish last.
The final persisted/displayed setting can be on rather than the latest off choice.
Alternatively switch projects before the first PATCH responds: its response overwrites the next project's local checkbox state.
item.surface: UE5 .zip > Auto-fix before export checkbox
item.title: Auto-fix can end in the wrong selected state or appear on the next project — toggle requests have no ordering or project-response guard

item.evidence: server.py:137-140 NodeGraphEdge stores only from_node/to_node/kind, not source/destination pin names. unrealExtras.js:59 filters edges to '(e.kind || "exec") === "exec"'; :63-64 chooses an output by edge iteration order rather than node.outputs or edge source identity; :62 only connects to 'execute'; :81 emits every generated pin with PinCategory="exec". Workspace.jsx:575-579 copies this output and zipExport.js:184 writes it to the plugin.
item.expected: request: "pasting into a Blueprint editor (Ctrl+V) creates the real nodes and wires" and "branches, variables (get/set), sequence and delays"; R-289/R-290 require preserving node and pin connections. Data edges, value pin types and branch output identities must survive export independently of array ordering.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts that a supported stored graph with a variable feeding a branch condition loses that data wire entirely. Branch outputs are assigned then/else solely by edge iteration order, with no stored pin identity to determine whether the first destination belongs to True or False. Developers cannot obtain the promised working nodes and wires; behavior can be reversed or disconnected, requiring manual graph reconstruction. No Unreal paste was executed.
reproduction_steps: Open a system whose graph includes a variable-get node feeding a Branch via a data edge.
Press Copy for Unreal, or export its plugin and inspect the Blueprint paste file.
The produced text contains no value/Condition connection.
For a branching graph, compare its desired output labels to export: edges are assigned then and else by list position, not their actual output pin.
item.surface: Event Graph > Copy for Unreal; plugin Blueprints/*_EventGraph.txt
item.title: Blueprint users lose data wires and branch semantics on paste — clipboard mapper discards data edges and pin identities

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:273 sends result as previous_system for Fix & regenerate. build_user_text(server.py:275) calls compact_system(req.previous_system,8000,full=True). compact_system(:251/:254) slices the header at 8,000 characters and source at 12,000, while synthesis replaces the workspace system (Workspace.jsx:227); no merge restores the omitted suffix afterward.
item.expected: R-312: regeneration "keeps the project's other modules and parameters"; server's exposed revision promise (server.py:216) also says keep unaffected content. checklist, AI and model features: trace truncation "that could remove essential meaning." Give the regenerating model the complete authoritative code or use a preservation mechanism for parts omitted from its context.
item.observed: AI and model features: a supported imported project with custom declarations beyond header character 8,000 or implementation beyond source character 12,000 loses that code from the structural-fix model's input even though the client supplied it. The returned full replacement is not merged with the original. Developers cannot rely on unrelated custom behavior surviving this operation; reviewing/recovering it requires manual comparison or restoring a saved version. This establishes omitted grounding, not an observation that a particular model actually deleted a particular function.
reproduction_steps: Import/open a project with an unrelated custom function/declaration after the 8k-header or 12k-source cutoff.
Use Fix & regenerate for a missing include near the start.
Trace the provider text: the unrelated suffix is absent.
The resulting full system replaces the original without restoring omitted regions.
item.surface: Compile check > Fix & regenerate for long/imported systems
item.title: Structural fixes cannot reliably preserve long custom code — regeneration silently truncates the previous system before the model call
